audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer's whys[] are shifted one stage from index 3 onward: the Levels 4-5 row explained level 6, the Level 6 row explained his first item, the First-item row explained two items, and the 2+ row explained 'late'. Every reader from Levels 4-5 down was getting the next stage's advice.
audit.why: The prose itself is correct about the lane — Levels 4-5 are Malphite's best stretch, level 6 hands it to Feast, and it never comes back. Only the mapping was wrong, and the content 'mid' paragraph ('Levels 4-5 are my best stretch') proves it.
audit.corrected: Rewrote whys[3] through whys[6] so each row explains its own stage.

audit.why: The spike placement is right and matches the 48.08% headline: Malphite peaks at levels 2-5 on Thunderclap armour and the Ground Slam slow, Cho'Gath takes over at 6 with Feast and never gives it back. Both layers say the same thing.

audit.whatIsWrong: Rupture was described only as 'telegraphed, dodge it', and Feral Scream only as 'silence'. Neither said what they actually do to Malphite's kit.
audit.why: Rupture is a 6s flat cooldown knockup — displacement, which is the one thing that stops Unstoppable Force, and he has it every six seconds. Feral Scream is an 11s cone at only 300 range, so the silence that blanks your R cast is avoidable purely on spacing. Those two facts are the whole level-6 fight.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d and dontsFull[1].d now state the knockup-stops-R interaction, the 6s clock and the 300-range cone.

audit.whatIsWrong: The 'Let him free-stack R' Don't had a body copy-pasted from the generic Granite Shield trade line and never mentioned Feast stacking.
audit.why: Feast is 80s at rank 1 and permanently grows his max health on a kill, which is also what makes his percent-health true damage bigger against a tank. Denying stacks is the actual instruction.
